dialect.detail: Micro Focus COBOL with free-format directive; originally VAX COBOL 1991, converted to Micro Focus COBOL 2002 per author comment. Uses Report Writer (RD/REPORT SECTION) and INDEXED file I/O.
evidence: ORGANIZATION IS INDEXED with ALTERNATE RECORD KEY
REPORT SECTION with RD, TYPE IS DETAIL, GROUP INDICATE
SET ... TO TRUE with 88-level condition names

purpose.domain_detail: Campus bookshop purchase requirements reporting system; matches books to publishers and lecturers for a given semester
purpose.summary: This program generates a Purchase Requirements Report for a campus bookshop. It reads indexed files for purchase requests, books, and publishers, filters by semester, and produces a formatted report using COBOL Report Writer showing publisher name, book title, quantity required, and lecturer name.

notable_features: COBOL Report Writer (REPORT SECTION, RD, TYPE IS DETAIL, TYPE IS PAGE HEADING, TYPE IS REPORT FOOTING, GROUP INDICATE, INITIATE/TERMINATE/GENERATE)
Multiple INDEXED files with ALTERNATE RECORD KEYs and DUPLICATES
ACCESS MODE IS DYNAMIC with START and sequential READ NEXT
88-level condition names used as flags (End-Of-Publishers, End-Of-Books, etc.)
Semester filtering logic in PROCEDURE DIVISION
Free-format source triggered by $ SET SOURCEFORMAT directive
DISPLAY statements used for debugging (bfstatus, PrStatus, etc.)
verdict.notes: Author is Michael Coughlan, a well-known COBOL educator; program ID and exam reference (DP291-91-EXAM) confirm this is an academic/educational exercise. Debug DISPLAY statements left in code. No lines exceed 72 columns; free format confirmed by compiler directive. Minor inconsistency: 'End-OF-Publishers' vs 'End-Of-Publishers' in SET statements (case-insensitive in COBOL).
